problem_motivation.content: The molten salt corrosion behavior of dual-phase high entropy alloys has not been reported, creating a gap in evaluating their application potential.
problem_motivation.evidence_span: However, their molten salt corrosion behavior has not been reported

problem_motivation.content: Degradation of structural materials in molten salt environments remains a critical concern for CSP systems, with high operating temperatures and reactive salts increasing corrosion susceptibility and reducing component lifetimes.
problem_motivation.evidence_span: However, degradation of structural materials in a molten salt environment remains a critical concern in CSP systems [ [9] , [10] ]. The high operating temperature and reactive nature of the salt significantly increase the corrosion susceptibility of the materials and reduce component lifetimes [ [4] ].

problem_motivation.content: The molten salt corrosion behavior of dual-phase HEAs and the fundamental understanding of underlying high-temperature corrosion mechanisms have not been reported.
problem_motivation.evidence_span: However, the molten salt corrosion behavior of dual phase HEAs for potential use in CSP systems has not been reported so far, and fundamental understanding of the underlying high-temperature corrosion mechanisms is lacking.

prior_approach.content: Previous studies have reported various EHEAs with excellent mechanical properties and some, like AlCoCrFeNi2.1, showed superior pitting corrosion resistance in chloride solutions at room temperature.
prior_approach.evidence_span: Some examples of EHEAs with excellent combination of strength and ductility include CoCrFeNiZr 0.5 , CoCrFeNiMnPd 1.4 , CoCrFeNiMnPd 0.6 , Nb 25 Sc 25 Ti 25 Zr 25 , AlCrFeNiMo 0.2 , Al 1.2 CrCuFeNi 2 and AlCoCrFeNi x [ [24] ]. In particular, the AlCoCrFeNi 2.1 EHEA with lamellar arrangement of BCC (B2) and FCC (L1 2 ) solid-solution phases has shown the most promising mechanical properties [ [22] , [25] , [26] , [27] ]. AlCoCrFeNi 2.1 EHEA showed superior pitting corrosion resistance compared to 304 stainless steel in chloride solution at room temperature [ [27] ]. This EHEA exhibited an excellent combination of high yield strength (~750 MPa) and ductility (elongation ~18%) at room temperature [ [22] , [28] ].

prior_approach.content: Dual-phase steels have been previously reported to have excellent corrosion resistance and a good combination of strength and ductility.
prior_approach.evidence_span: Dual-phase steels have been reported to have excellent corrosion resistance and a good combination of strength and ductility [ [29] , [30] , [31] , [32] , [33] , [34] , [35] ].

prior_approach.content: Scanning Kelvin Probe (SKP) analysis has been utilized in prior work to measure the relative electron work function to explain microstructure effects.
prior_approach.evidence_span: To explain the effect of eutectic microstructure on the local electrochemical activity, Scanning Kelvin Probe (SKP) analysis was utilized to measure the relative electron work function [ [27] , [36] , [37] ].

prior_limitation.content: The current study did not evaluate how moisture content affects corrosion behavior, identifying a gap in the experimental scope.
prior_limitation.evidence_span: However, a detailed evaluation of the effect of moisture content on corrosion behavior has not been performed in the current study

prior_limitation.content: Previous literature indicates that Fe-based alloys suffer from poor stability at elevated temperatures in molten chloride media due to the dissolution of Cr and Fe.
prior_limitation.evidence_span: Poor stability of Fe-based alloys at elevated temperatures in molten chloride media due to dissolution of Cr and Fe has been reported previously

prior_limitation.content: Prior studies report that duplex steel suffers from severe chloride-induced corrosion due to the preferential attack of its ferrite phase.
prior_limitation.evidence_span: At 650 °C, duplex steel has been reported to show chloride-induced severe corrosion due to preferential attack of its ferrite phase

mechanism_principle.content: The selective dissolution is explained by micro-galvanic coupling between the phases.
mechanism_principle.evidence_span: This was attributed to micro-galvanic coupling between the two phases in each alloy

mechanism_principle.content: The protective effect is explained by the FCC-L12 phase acting as a barrier due to increased work function.
mechanism_principle.evidence_span: Additionally, the work function increased with increasing temperature for AlCoCrFeNi 2.1, indicating that the FCC-L1 2 phase acted as a barrier against further oxidation and protected the underlying BCC-B2 phase

mechanism_principle.content: The observed superior corrosion resistance is attributed to the presence of aluminum in the EHEA, which hinders the dissolution of other alloy constituents.
mechanism_principle.evidence_span: This may be attributed to the presence of Al in AlCoCrFeNi 2.1 that hinders the dissolution of the other alloy constituents in the molten salt

evidence_result.content: The EHEA exhibited a significantly lower corrosion rate than the conventional steel at 450°C.
evidence_result.evidence_span: The EHEA showed a significantly lower corrosion rate of ~1 mm/year at 450 °C compared to ~8 mm/year for DS2205

evidence_result.content: The EHEA exhibited a significantly lower corrosion rate than the conventional steel at 650°C.
evidence_result.evidence_span: Similarly, EHEA showed a lower corrosion rate of ~9 mm/year at 650 °C compared to ~20 mm/year for DS2205

constraint.content: The ratio of counter electrode surface area to working electrode surface area was strictly fixed to ensure valid electrochemical measurements.
constraint.evidence_span: The surface area ratio of the counter electrode (CE) to the working electrode (WE) was kept fixed at 1

constraint.content: The work function measurements were constrained to a specific tip-to-sample separation distance.
constraint.evidence_span: Work function was determined at a tip to sample separation of 50 µm
